subject: card 219 retro pick, an assumption line with a probe in the slice of any card that changes a rule, the ranking or the checker
result: PASSED round 1 (3 Yes, 3 Support-it), confirmed by the independent re-run (3 Yes, 3 Support-it)
claude_seat_reason: probes show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota

round1.reply:
Yes

P1 (Pick/hypothesis): The pick is tied to a concrete product harm, two signed-off cards held for about 55 minutes, and it has a measurable target of 2 to 0.
P2 (C1): The rule applies only to cards that change a rule, the ranking or the checker. Other cards carry no cost, so it is not over-specified up front.
P3 (C2): The architect writes the line and the reviewer checks the probe. Each role works in its own context, and an unprobed line gets checked first.
P4 (C3): "No invariant change" is a single line with no new file, seat or meeting. That keeps the overhead small.
P5 (C4): The rule stays a slice line and does not blur into D157, D158 or D165. This follows the no-blur rule.
P6 (Metric and counter-metrics): The metric comes from git and has a target of 0. The counter-metrics (slice minutes, unprobed lines, ceremony) are evidence, not targets, so they do not invite Goodhart gaming.
P7 (Trial scope): The trial covers 3 matching cards, and the retro decides keep, revise or drop. Removal happens only at the retro, as the standing rules require.
P8 (Accountability): A matching card without the line counts as not run, and the auditor tick may FAIL it. An open FAIL stops the line, consistent with the standing rules.
P9 (Baseline and no-blur scoring): The card 219 baseline is concrete, and each retro scores each rule on its own record.
P10 (Reversibility): It is a two-way door. Deleting the slice line undoes it and no shared state changes.

Support-it

P1 (the pick): Sound and minimal. It checks the invariant at the change site, and the card 219 record shows the failure it targets.

P2 (C1, the slice line): One line per invariant, capped at three, with a probe. That is cheap and testable. Whether a card "changes a rule, the ranking or the checker" is a judgment call, so the architect's classification will vary at the edges.

P3 (C2, who checks): The reviewer checks the probe, and an "unprobed" label gives review a concrete thing to look for. A probe has to be something someone actually ran, because the git-only audit can't confirm that it was.

P4 (C3, no new file, seat or meeting): Good. "No invariant change" is a cheap default for cards outside C1.

P5 (C4, no blur with D157, D158, D165): Clear boundaries, and each rule keeps its own metric.

P6 (metric and counter-metrics): The held-cards metric is measurable from git. The ceremony counter-metric is the one most likely to show false positives, so the trial retro should sample it by hand.

P7 (accountability check): A matching card with no line counts as not run, and the git check is objective. The rule is only as good as how well "matches C1" is defined, so the trial retro should record borderline cards.

P8 (reversibility): Two-way door. Deleting the slice line is enough to undo it.
